note: Recorded from a physical ST-LINK/V2 attached to an STM32F1-class target by the hwlab stlink plugin (native Go usbfs; no OpenOCD, STM32CubeProgrammer, st-flash, libusb, Python or CGO). Metadata and hashes only: no firmware bytes, no unique-ID words, no real USB serial (replaced by 38FFAABBCCDDEEFF00112233). The replayable session is ../real-stlink-stm32-flash.

target.identification_confidence: family: high (DBGMCU dev id, 1 KB pages, option-byte layout, FLASH controller behaviour); exact part number: not determined
target.flash_size_register_0x1FFFF7E0: 0xFFFF (blank); the 128 KB is the readable window (0x08020000 faults), reported as flash_size_source=probed
target.nrst: not observed through the 20-pin connection (no reset seen after the pin pulse): NOT claimed

flash.cycle: backup x2 identical -> erase page 0 -> program -> verify -> reset -> counter advances (0x00058507 -> 0x000b0eef in 500 ms) -> 100 single steps -> breakpoint at work() -> write watchpoint on the counter -> restore -> whole-flash re-read hash == original

results.single_step_note: acceptance firmware: every PC followed the program order (16- and 32-bit instructions); the SRAM counter equalled the number of executed str instructions
results.sram_write_restore: 8/16/32-bit and unaligned, restored byte for byte, invalid addresses refused
results.reset: system and core reset observed (PC at the reset vector after reset-halt; the vector is read AFTER the reset because the original firmware relocates VTOR); NRST pin not claimed

throughput.flash_program_note: 8 pages, each erased, programmed through the SRAM halfword loader and read back; dominated by page erase and verify reads
throughput.sram_64KiB: not measurable: the target has 20 KB of SRAM

unplug_replug.rediscovery: by USB serial; identity (DP IDCODE, CPUID) unchanged, memory read and halt/resume OK
unplug_replug.aborted_attempt: one earlier run timed out because the probe was not plugged back in inside its 15-minute window; it was not counted
